source_claims: Thompson (1917) On Growth and Form, 1st edition -- every claim dated 1917
relation_taxonomy: REFUTED | PARTIALLY_REFUTED | SUPPORTED | MIXED | SUPERSEDED | QUALIFIED | NO_DIRECT_TEST | NOT_TESTABLE

T1917-001.claim: The form of an organism is a 'diagram of forces': form can and should be described physically and mathematically, in terms of the forces that produced it.
T1917-001.literature_citation: Gould, S.J. (1971) 'D'Arcy Thompson and the science of form' (essay; repr. in Gould 1977, Ever Since Darwin)
T1917-001.counterclaim: No counterclaim is possible against a programme. Gould's influential qualification: physical forces are real but form is also shaped by evolutionary history and contingency -- 'form as diagram of forces' is incomplete, not false.

T1917-002.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. I + Epilogue, pp. 1-15; Epilogue, Figs. -
T1917-002.claim: Many forms are explained by physical forces directly and do not require (and are not well explained by) adaptation/heredity acting part-by-part; related forms differ by whole-form transformation rather than by independent change of parts.
T1917-002.literature_citation: Gould (1971); Gould & Lewontin (1979) Proc. R. Soc. B 205:581-598 (spandrels paper)
T1917-002.counterclaim: Thompson's anti-adaptationist, whole-form programme was first celebrated (Gould 1971, which revived him), then qualified by Gould himself: from the 1980s he refuted Thompson's mechanical determinism in favour of historical contingency and 'tinkering'. Modern synthesis: constraints (Thompson's half) and selection both operate; neither alone explains form.

T1917-003.claim: Surface grows as L^2 and volume/weight as L^3, so surface:volume falls as 1/L; this alone bounds organism size and forces disproportionate change of parts with size.
T1917-003.literature_citation: Kleiber, M. (1932) Hilgardia 6:315-353; Glazier, D.S. (2022) Proc. R. Soc. B 289:20221605
T1917-003.counterclaim: The surface-law application (metabolism proportional to surface, M^2/3) was countered by Kleiber (1932): basal metabolic rate scales as ~M^3/4, not M^2/3. Glazier (2022) counters both: exponents are variable and context-dependent -- there is no universal 2/3 or 3/4. The pure geometry (area L^2, volume L^3) is not in dispute; its use as a metabolic law is.
T1917-003.quantitative_margin: Exponent dispute: 0.67 (surface law) vs 0.73-0.75 (Kleiber 1932) vs 'no universal exponent' (Glazier 2022)

T1917-004.claim: Strength of a support scales with cross-sectional area (L^2) while load scales with weight (L^3), so larger land animals must be relatively thicker-boned / differently proportioned (Galilean scaling).
T1917-004.who_and_when: McMahon (1973); Schmidt-Nielsen (1984) and later allometry literature
T1917-004.literature_citation: McMahon, T.A. (1973) Science 179:1201-1204 (elastic similarity); Schmidt-Nielsen, K. (1984) Scaling: Why Is Animal Size So Important?
T1917-004.counterclaim: Pure geometric similarity (strength L^2 vs weight L^3) does not describe real skeletons; McMahon's elastic-similarity (buckling) criterion predicts different, often better-fitting proportions. Thompson's scaling dilemma is real, his implied geometric solution is not the one animals use in general.
T1917-004.quantitative_margin: Elastic similarity predicts diameter proportional to length^1.5 (vs geometric proportionality); fits many trees/limbs better, neither fits all

T1917-005.claim: Different physics dominates at different magnitudes: surface tension and viscosity rule small organisms, gravity and inertia rule large ones; there is a least size of organism set by molecular/thermal scales.
T1917-005.literature_citation: Vogel, S. (1994) Life in Moving Fluids, 2nd ed.; Purcell (1977) Am. J. Phys. 45:3-11
T1917-005.counterclaim: No substantive counterclaim. Purcell (1977) made Thompson's small-scale regime famous ('life at low Reynolds number'): viscosity, not inertia, rules the small -- exactly Thompson's magnitude argument, quantified.

T1917-006.claim: Cell (e.g. nerve-cell) size is roughly independent of the size of the animal; larger animals have more cells, not proportionally larger cells.
T1917-006.who_and_when: Modern cell-size literature (e.g. Marshall et al. 2012)
T1917-006.literature_citation: Marshall, W.F. et al. (2012) Curr. Biol. 22:R256-R260 ('What determines cell size?')
T1917-006.counterclaim: Broadly right, with named exceptions Thompson did not treat: some neurons, eggs, syncytia and polyploid cells scale with organism/ploidy. Cell size is actively regulated, not a passive constant.

T1917-007.claim: Growth in size/weight over time follows a definite, plottable curve: rapid (near-compound-interest) early growth with a steadily diminishing specific rate of growth.
T1917-007.literature_citation: von Bertalanffy, L. (1957) Q. Rev. Biol. 32:217-231
T1917-007.counterclaim: Thompson's plotted growth curves are descriptive. Von Bertalanffy replaced curve-description with a mechanistic balance law (dW/dt = anabolism - catabolism) that predicts the curve family. Later qualification: the 'universal' 2/3 exponent in that law is not universal -- optimally fitted exponents vary widely; the von Bertalanffy function is 'weakly universal' for fish, not for non-fish (PeerJ 2018, 'On the exponent in the Von Bertalanffy growth model').
T1917-007.quantitative_margin: Superseded as method, not refuted as data: no single growth curve/exponent fits all taxa

T1917-008.claim: Parts of an organism grow at different but definite relative rates, so form changes systematically with size; the changing proportions of organs (brain, heart, body; plaice weight-length) are growth-rate phenomena.
T1917-008.who_and_when: Huxley (1932) formalised it; Royal Society discussion (1950) and Gould (1966) qualified it
T1917-008.literature_citation: Huxley, J.S. (1932) Problems of Relative Growth; Needham, Zuckerman et al. (1950) Proc. R. Soc. B 137:465-525; Gould, S.J. (1966) Biol. Rev. 41:587-640
T1917-008.counterclaim: SUPPORTING: Huxley (1932) turned Thompson's differential-growth claim into the allometric law y = b x^k. COUNTER (1950): the allometry equation cannot simultaneously hold between two parts and the whole, and often only fits as piecewise straight lines -- so its constants are 'a rough and ready shorthand of description', not physiological entities. Fitting the law does not prove a growth-rate mechanism.
T1917-008.quantitative_margin: Huxley's k = ratio of specific growth rates; the 1950 objection is logical (inconsistent between part-part and part-whole fits), not a percentage

T1917-009.claim: Rate of growth varies lawfully with temperature and shows daily/seasonal/annual periodicity, recorded e.g. in tree growth (Douglass) and plant/root growth curves.
T1917-009.literature_citation: Douglass, A.E. (1919+) dendrochronology; standard growth-physiology literature thereafter
T1917-009.counterclaim: No counterclaim; this became dendrochronology and quantitative growth physiology. Included for completeness: a Thompson claim the literature absorbed rather than fought.

T1917-010.claim: Regeneration restores form at a measurable rate related to the amount removed (Durbin/Ellis tail-regeneration curves), i.e. restoration of form is itself a lawful growth process.
T1917-010.literature_citation: Modern regeneration literature exists (urodele limb, planarian) but does not re-test Thompson/Durbin/Ellis's amount-removed vs time-restored relation on his system
T1917-010.counterclaim: No published counterclaim found. Absence of a test is the finding: this 1917 claim is still open.

T1917-011.claim: The mitotic figure behaves as a system of forces between two poles: spindle and aster configurations, and chromosome movements, follow the lines of a bipolar field of force (with Peddie's magnetic-field diagrams as the physical analogue).
T1917-011.literature_citation: Mitchison, T. & Kirschner, M. (1984) Nature 312:237-242 (dynamic instability / search-and-capture); McIntosh, J.R. (2012) 'Motors or dynamics: what really moves chromosomes?'
T1917-011.counterclaim: Thompson/Peddie's bipolar field-of-force mechanism is not the mechanism. The spindle is a self-organising microtubule machine: dynamic instability (1984) lets microtubules search-and-capture chromosomes, and depolymerisation itself generates poleward force with no motor and no ATP (shown in vitro from 1988). The bipolar *geometry* Thompson drew was right; the force-field physics was replaced.

T1917-012.claim: Early cleavage/segmentation patterns of eggs conform to the same bipolar (two-like-pole) field configuration.
T1917-012.literature_citation: Cleavage is now explained by spindle positioning and cortical mechanics (modern cell-biology literature)
T1917-012.counterclaim: No direct literature test of Thompson's two-like-pole field reading of cleavage patterns. The modern mechanism (spindle position -> cleavage furrow) makes the field picture unnecessary, which is a supersession by neglect, not a refutation.

T1917-013.claim: A free, isolated cell (like a liquid drop) tends to the spherical/minimal-area form under surface tension, departing from it only under identifiable constraints.
T1917-013.who_and_when: Heer et al. / Lecuit-group reviews (2017); Fischer-Friedrich et al. (2014)
T1917-013.literature_citation: 'Tension, contraction and tissue morphogenesis' (2017, PMC5769629), Box 1 'A note about surface tension'
T1917-013.counterclaim: Directly addressed to Thompson (1917): 'While D'Arcy Thompson dismissed the connection between surface tension and contractility, we now understand that this connection is paramount... the tension at cell surfaces is NOT driven by surface tension, as Thompson understood it, but by tension in the cortical actin layer.' Membrane tension's contribution to effective surface tension is often negligible. The sphere-as-null survives; Thompson's passive-liquid mechanism does not.
T1917-013.quantitative_margin: Mechanism refuted; spherical null shape retained as approximation

T1917-014.claim: The forms of single cells and cell-like organisms (Plateau's oil globules; Lagena and other forams/protists) are surfaces of revolution from the minimal-surface catalogue: sphere, cylinder, unduloid, nodoid, catenoid.
T1917-014.who_and_when: Modern cell-mechanics comparisons (e.g. PLOS Comput. Biol. 2023, cell shape vs minimal surfaces)
T1917-014.literature_citation: 'Modelling cell shape in 3D structured environments' (2023) PLOS Comput. Biol. 19:e1011412
T1917-014.counterclaim: Constant-mean-curvature (Plateau/Delaunay) shapes are a good model for suspended cells and a measurably wrong one for adherent/structured cells: observed-vs-minimised shape discrepancy is large in L- and V-shaped micropatterns (spectral amplitude difference ~0.15-0.18) and small in triangular patterns (~0.03). Thompson's catalogue is a limiting case, not the general rule.
T1917-014.quantitative_margin: Discrepancy ~0.15-0.18 (L/V patterns) vs ~0.03 (triangular): context decides, contra a universal surface-tension law

T1917-015.claim: A liquid cylinder breaks up into a row of spheres (Plateau-Rayleigh instability), and the same segmentation is seen in protoplasmic threads/cells.
T1917-015.who_and_when: Rayleigh (1878, pre-Thompson physics Thompson applied); confirmed in modern fluid mechanics
T1917-015.literature_citation: Lord Rayleigh (1878) on liquid-jet/cylinder instability; standard texts thereafter
T1917-015.counterclaim: No counterclaim to the physics (Thompson was applying Rayleigh/Plateau, not originating it). Biological instances remain case-by-case demonstrations, not a tested general law of protoplasm.
T1917-015.quantitative_margin: Instability criterion (disturbances with wavelength exceeding the cylinder circumference grow) is textbook

T1917-016.claim: Cell form changes lawfully with the density/osmotic strength of the medium (Koltzoff's decapod sperm cells in saline solutions), as a surface-tension/osmotic system should.
T1917-016.literature_citation: Modern osmotic cell mechanics exists but is not a replication of Koltzoff's decapod-sperm experiment as Thompson cited it
T1917-016.counterclaim: No published counterclaim or direct replication found. Open.

T1917-017.claim: Adsorption concentrates dissolved substances at surfaces/interfaces, and this physical concentration helps explain localisation and pattern within the cell/organism.
T1917-017.counterclaim: Too general to have attracted a testable counterclaim. Its specific descendants (surface catalysis, membrane localisation) were settled case by case.

T1917-018.claim: Cells in contact, like soap films, meet three-at-a-time at ~120 degrees and in other respects obey Plateau's laws of film configuration.
T1917-018.who_and_when: Farhadifar et al. (2007); vertex-model literature thereafter
T1917-018.literature_citation: Farhadifar, R. et al. (2007) Curr. Biol. 17:2095-2104 (Drosophila wing epithelium vertex model)
T1917-018.counterclaim: Plateau-style junction laws hold as the energy-minimising limit of vertex models, but real epithelia are active: measured junction angles and cell shapes deviate systematically, and the deviations carry the biology (proliferation, contractility). Thompson's 120-degree rule is the passive limit, not the tissue's operating point.

T1917-019.claim: Tissue cells tessellate approximately as hexagons / as a froth, the configuration that partitions area with least perimeter.
T1917-019.who_and_when: Gibson et al. (2006); Farhadifar et al. (2007)
T1917-019.literature_citation: Gibson, M.C. et al. (2006) Nature 442:1038-1041; Farhadifar et al. (2007)
T1917-019.counterclaim: Epithelial polygon distributions are froth-like but *not* simply 'hexagons tile best': proliferating epithelia have a characteristic polygon spectrum (substantial pentagon/heptagon fractions) explained by division topology, not by perimeter minimisation alone. Thompson's froth analogy survives, his implied hexagonal optimum does not describe growing tissue.
T1917-019.quantitative_margin: Real epithelia: hexagons are only the modal class (~40-50% in the wing disc), with large 5- and 7-sided fractions

T1917-020.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. VII, pp. 293-345, Figs. 136-175 (with Ch. VIII)
T1917-020.claim: Sachs's rules describe cell division in plant tissues: daughter cells tend to equal volume, new walls meet old walls at right angles and follow minimal-area configurations.
T1917-020.literature_citation: Errera (1888) origin; modern tests in meristem imaging literature
T1917-020.counterclaim: No substantive counterclaim; Sachs/Errera rules survive in refined, mechanically informed form. Thompson was reporting and endorsing Sachs, and the literature kept the rule, not the refutation.

T1917-021.claim: The bee's honeycomb - hexagonal prisms closed by three rhombi meeting at the Maraldi angle (~109 deg 28 min) - is the configuration using least wax for the capacity (the isoperimetric claim).
T1917-021.literature_citation: Fejes Toth, L. (1964) Bull. AMS 70:468-481, 'What the bees know and what they do not know'; Hales, T.C. (2001) Ann. of Math. 153 (honeycomb conjecture proved)
T1917-021.counterclaim: SPLIT VERDICT, and the split is the famous one. (a) The hexagonal tiling IS optimal -- proved by Hales (2001): Thompson/Pappus right. (b) The bees' three-rhombi cell base is NOT the wax-minimum: Fejes Toth (1964) built a better base (two hexagons + two rhombi). Thompson's 'least wax' claim is therefore wrong in its 3D detail. Fejes Toth himself adds that the saving is practically illusory.
T1917-021.quantitative_margin: Better base saves <0.35% of the area of a cell opening (much less of total cell surface) -- Fejes Toth (1964); a 2025 re-optimisation puts the total available saving at ~0.50%

T1917-022.claim: Isoperimetric/minimal-area principles also govern other hollow and aggregate structures he treats in this chapter (e.g. radiolarian-like and echinoderm larval skeletal arrangements, vessel and tissue partitions).
T1917-022.who_and_when: Weaire & Phelan (1994) for the foam instance
T1917-022.literature_citation: Weaire, D. & Phelan, R. (1994) Phil. Mag. Lett. 69:107-110
T1917-022.counterclaim: Catch-all row: no single literature verdict. For its foam instance there IS a precise counterclaim: Kelvin's supposedly minimal equal-volume cell (the structure Thompson's generation took as the minimal partition) is beaten by the Weaire-Phelan structure. Split this row per structure before citing any verdict.
T1917-022.quantitative_margin: Weaire-Phelan uses ~0.3% less surface area than Kelvin's cell (1994)

T1917-023.claim: Concretions and calcospherites grow by radial deposition about a centre (Harting's artificial concretions in egg albumen mimic natural ones), giving concentric/spherical forms by physical deposition alone.
T1917-023.literature_citation: Harting's artificial-spherite analogy is cited historically; no modern quantitative re-test of radial-deposition geometry on Thompson's examples was found

T1917-024.claim: Sponge and alcyonarian spicule forms (needles, tri-/tetraradiates and their aggregates) are the forms physical deposition/crystallisation takes within the cell/field that secretes them.
T1917-024.literature_citation: Modern spicule literature is biomineralisation/genetic (silicateins, etc.), not a test of Thompson's deposition-geometry claim
T1917-024.counterclaim: No direct test found. The modern mechanism literature (protein-guided silica deposition) supersedes the purely physical picture without ever scoring his ray-angle geometry.

T1917-025.claim: Radiolarian and similar siliceous skeletons approximate geodesic/minimal frameworks on a sphere (latticed shells as systems of shortest lines and near-equal partitions).
T1917-025.literature_citation: Haeckel's radiolarian geometry is much reproduced, rarely measured against geodesic/minimal predictions
T1917-025.counterclaim: No published counterclaim or quantitative test found. Open -- and, unusually, still open after a century.

T1917-026.claim: Geodesic (shortest-line) trajectories on a curved surface explain the courses of spicules, shell sculpture and other skeletal lines laid down on that surface.
T1917-026.counterclaim: A principle, not a tested claim: no literature verdict exists until it is instantiated in one system (trabeculae are the instance with a verdict -- see T1917-037).

T1917-027.claim: Spiral shells (and other gnomonic-growth structures) are logarithmic (equiangular) spirals: the wharves enlarge by a constant ratio, so the form is unchanged by growth (r proportional to e^{k theta}).
T1917-027.literature_citation: Raup, D.M. (1966) J. Paleontol. 40:1178-1190; Raup & Michelson (1965) Science 147
T1917-027.counterclaim: Raup did not refute the logarithmic spiral; he demoted it from law to coordinate system. Real shells need three parameters (W whorl expansion, D, T) plus a generating-curve shape, parameters can drift during growth, and large regions of the possible morphospace are empty -- which a pure log-spiral law does not explain. Modern spiral-fitting (2021, 'Refined methods for estimating spirals', doi:10.26879/1071) needs 12 spiral types and treats 'spiral deviation' as the informative signal: exact log-spiral growth is the null, not the finding.
T1917-027.quantitative_margin: 3+ Raup parameters replace Thompson's single spiral constant; deviations from log growth are systematic, not noise

T1917-028.claim: In Nautilus the shell spiral and the septa bear the stated geometric relations (septa meeting the wall, spiral as evolute/involute relations he diagrams).
T1917-028.literature_citation: Nautilus buoyancy/CT literature (e.g. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.fc4vf, chambered-shell CT) measures function, not Thompson's septum/spiral geometry
T1917-028.counterclaim: No direct test of his stated septal relations found. Open (and cheap to close -- see dataset audit).

T1917-029.claim: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.
T1917-029.literature_citation: Foraminiferal morphometrics exists (e.g. fusulinid heterochrony, Dryad 10.5061/dryad.sn02v6x26) but does not test constant chamber-ratio generation on Brady's genera

T1917-030.claim: Single-chambered foraminiferal tests (Lagena etc.) take the surface-tension forms of Ch. V (flask/unduloid-like surfaces of revolution), chamber form preceding spiral coiling.
T1917-030.literature_citation: As T1917-014 (single-cell surface-tension forms), but never fitted to Lagena specifically
T1917-030.counterclaim: No direct test found. The general qualification of T1917-014 (active cortex, context-dependent fit) would apply if the geometry fit at all.

T1917-031.claim: Horns (ram, goat, Ovis ammon) are logarithmic spirals wound on a cone (a conical helicoid generated by gnomonic growth), differing between species by the spiral constants and torsion.
T1917-031.literature_citation: Horn literature is investment/sexual-selection focused (e.g. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.fxpnvx16w), not conical-log-spiral fitting
T1917-031.counterclaim: No published test of horns as conical logarithmic helicoids, Thompson-style, was found. Open.

T1917-032.claim: Teeth and tusks grow by the same spiral/torsion geometry (with St Venant torsion curves describing the twisted prismatic forms).

T1917-033.claim: Leaf/floret divergence approximates the golden (Fibonacci) angle (~137.5 deg), with rational approximations 1/2, 1/3, 2/5, 3/8... and Fibonacci numbers of parastichies.
T1917-033.literature_citation: Douady, S. & Couder, Y. (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 68:2098-2101
T1917-033.counterclaim: No counterclaim -- the opposite. Douady & Couder produced Fibonacci phyllotaxis and the golden angle (~137.5 deg) in a purely physical system (repelling ferrofluid drops), with no botanical machinery: the pattern is what a self-organising repulsive system does. This supports Thompson's physicalist reading and refutes only the mystical/numerological readings Thompson himself disliked.
T1917-033.quantitative_margin: Golden angle 137.5 deg and Fibonacci parastichies emerge from one control parameter (drop periodicity) in vitro (1992)

T1917-034.claim: Birds' (and other hard-shelled) eggs are solids of revolution whose meridian curves form a definite, species-varying family of ovoids, comparable geometrically across species.
T1917-034.who_and_when: Stoddard et al. (2017); Birkhead et al. (2019); Narushin et al. (2021)
T1917-034.literature_citation: Stoddard, M.C. et al. (2017) Science 356:1249-1254; Birkhead, T.R. et al. (2019) Ibis 161; Narushin, V.G. et al. (2021) Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. (universal egg formula)
T1917-034.counterclaim: Thompson's descriptive ovoid family was superseded twice over. (1) Mechanism: Stoddard et al. (2017), 49,000 eggs / 1,400 species -- egg shape is set by the membrane (pressure/stiffness), and correlates with flight ability; but flight explains little, and Birkhead et al. (2019) counter-counterclaim that incubation site/posture explains 70-85% in alcids/penguins. (2) Description: a 2021 'universal' egg formula with 4 parameters now does the describing. Nobody's ovoid curve, Thompson's included, is the standard anymore.
T1917-034.quantitative_margin: Flight (hand-wing index) explains only ~4% of egg-shape variation (Stoddard 2017, as re-analysed); incubation site >60%, models 70-85% (Birkhead 2019) -- Thompson's geometry-only account has no explanatory variable at all

T1917-035.claim: Certain hollow structures (e.g. sea-urchin tests diagrammed in Fig. 328, skulls and other shells) take forms explicable as membranes/shells under pressure and tension.
T1917-035.counterclaim: Too broad as stated to have a literature verdict. Split first (urchin test is the measurable instance).

T1917-036.claim: In a bent beam there is a neutral zone/axis free of tension and compression, and animal/plant structures that bend (bones, stems, trunks) are disposed accordingly (material where the stress is).
T1917-036.who_and_when: Standard beam theory (engineering consensus, before and after 1917)
T1917-036.literature_citation: Standard mechanics of materials (beam theory), before and after 1917
T1917-036.counterclaim: None: neutral-axis beam mechanics was settled engineering when Thompson wrote and remains so. The biological allocation claim bundled with it is T1917-037/038.

T1917-037.claim: Trabecular bone is arranged along the principal stress trajectories of the bone, as in Culmann's crane-head diagram applied to the human femur (the trajectorial theory).
T1917-037.who_and_when: Venieratos et al. (1987) FOR; Skedros & Baucom (2007) AGAINST the strict form
T1917-037.literature_citation: Venieratos et al. (1987), human femur (PubMed 3631524); Skedros, J.G. & Baucom, S.L. (2007) J. Theor. Biol. 244 (doi:10.1016/j.jtbi.2006.06.029)
T1917-037.counterclaim: The trajectorial theory (Wolff/Culmann, endorsed by Thompson, Fig. 335) has a split quantitative verdict. FOR: in frontal sections of human femora, trabecular direction converges on principal stress direction with a mean divergence of only +/-7 deg, better where stress is higher (1987). AGAINST the strict form: femoral-neck trabecular systems are systematically NON-orthogonal (~70 deg, not the 90 deg orthogonal trajectories the theory requires), and non-orthogonal (~60 deg) alignment cuts shear coupling by 33-75% under multidirectional loading -- i.e. real bone beats Thompson/Wolff's predicted arrangement at the real task.
T1917-037.quantitative_margin: +/-7 deg alignment (support, 1987) vs ~70 deg instead of 90 deg intersections and 33-75% shear-coupling advantage of the non-Thompson arrangement (2007)

T1917-038.claim: Hollow cylindrical construction (long bones, stems, quills) gives near-maximal strength/stiffness for weight, and branching systems (blood vessels, Fig. 329-330 after Hess; trees) branch at angles/ratios that economise work/material.
T1917-038.literature_citation: Murray, C.D. (1926) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 12:207-214 and J. Gen. Physiol. 9:835-841
T1917-038.counterclaim: Thompson (following Hess) stated branching-angle rules qualitatively. Murray (1926) replaced them with a derived optimum: minimum-work branching requires parent radius cubed = sum of daughter radii cubed (r0^3 = r1^3 + r2^3), with angles following from the radii -- and showed Hess's angle rule (Thompson's source) was incomplete because it ignored the continuing parent vessel. Not a refutation of Thompson's economy idea; its replacement by a computable law, nine years later.
T1917-038.quantitative_margin: Murray's law r0^3 = r1^3 + r2^3 (1926); minimum theoretical bifurcation angle 75 deg for vessels

T1917-039.claim: GENERAL THESIS: the form of a related species/genus can be obtained from another by a simple, continuous deformation of the whole coordinate system (a transformation of the whole form), rather than by unrelated changes of separate parts.
T1917-039.who_and_when: Bookstein (1977, 1978, 1989, and again 2023); Scholtz, Knotel & Baum (2020)
T1917-039.literature_citation: Bookstein, F.L. (1977) Math. Biosci. 34:177-219; (1978) Comput. Biol. Med.; (1989) IEEE TPAMI 11:567-585; (2023) Evol. Biol.; Scholtz et al. (2020) Zoomorphology 139 (doi:10.1007/s00435-020-00494-1)
T1917-039.counterclaim: The most consequential counterclaim in this registry, in three instalments. (1) Bookstein (1977): as *method*, Thompson's grids are 'as intractable as they seemed in 1917' -- hand-drawn, unfitted, generating no offspring; Thompson 'rests with the possibility of a single system of forces... he was content to exemplify'. (2) Bookstein (1989) supplied the missing method (thin-plate spline: exact, least-bending, decomposable), which is why modern grids are computed, not drawn. (3) Bookstein (2023) then countered his own tradition: exact TPS/Procrustes grids can mislead, and residual-leaving polynomial trend grids often interpret better -- so 'exact fit' is not the final court either. Separately, Scholtz et al. (2020) tested Thompson's own crab example in 3D and found only simple transformations congruent (see T1917-043).
T1917-039.quantitative_margin: Method superseded (1989 TPS is exact at landmarks by construction, vs Thompson's unfitted hand grid); but exactness != predictive superiority (2023 qualification). General-thesis verdict must be per-pair -- see repo 2026 horizon result (registry T1917-050)

T1917-040.claim: Human (and animal) heads/faces and proportions, in the Durer/Camper tradition, are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation; differences of facial angle/proportion are whole-grid deformations.
T1917-040.who_and_when: Bookstein (1977) on the grid method generally
T1917-040.literature_citation: Bookstein (1977) Math. Biosci. 34:177-219 covers Durer/Camper-style grids as part of the general intractability critique
T1917-040.counterclaim: No test of Thompson's Durer-derived human proportion grids as such. The general method critique (T1917-039) applies.

T1917-041.claim: Lanceolate, ovate and cordate leaves are transforms of one another under radial (polar) coordinates about an arrest/base point; the Begonia leaf is an instance of the same radial system.
T1917-041.counterclaim: No literature test of lanceolate->ovate->cordate leaf transformation under radial coordinates was found. (The repo has tested Thompson's Fig. 359 radial-cordate *formula* on ant heads -- an analogue, not this claim; see registry.) Open.

T1917-042.claim: The copepods Oithona nana and Sapphirina are related by a (logarithmic/coordinate) transformation of the whole form.
T1917-042.counterclaim: No published test of the Oithona->Sapphirina pair was found. The repo's 2026 test (84.2% vs 20.4% box, on his drawings) is REPO, not literature -- see the generated document's repo column.

T1917-043.claim: The carapaces of crabs (Geryon, Corystes, Scyramathia/Rochinia, Paralomis/Lithodes, Lupa/Portunus, Chorinus etc.) are mutually transformable by rectilinear-to-curvilinear coordinate transformation.
T1917-043.literature_citation: Scholtz, G., Knotel, D. & Baum, D. (2020) Zoomorphology (doi:10.1007/s00435-020-00494-1), 'D'Arcy W. Thompson's Cartesian transformations: a critical evaluation'
T1917-043.counterclaim: THE direct literature counterclaim to a Thompson figure. Using Thompson's drawings AND laser-scanned real carapaces (50 micrometre surface scans, projected to silhouettes, 8 landmarks): 'Only the simple transformations show a reasonable form of congruence. In particular, the transformations to majoid spider crabs reveal a complicated transformation of grids with partly crossing lines.' Accurate matching needs increasingly complex, non-Cartesian transformations -- undermining Thompson's simple explanatory model. Curious exception: the lithodid (convergent hermit-crab descendant) transforms easily. Note Thompson also silently included Paralomis, which is not a true crab at all.
T1917-043.quantitative_margin: Qualitative-geometric verdict (crossing grid lines = failed diffeomorphism in the majoid cases), on both his drawings and real 3D-scanned carapaces (2020)

T1917-044.claim: The amphipods Harpinia, Stegocephalus and Hyperia galba form a transformation series under coordinate deformation.
T1917-044.counterclaim: No published test of the amphipod series found. (Scholtz et al. 2020 tested the adjacent crab figure, not this one.) Open.

T1917-045.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish I), pp. 748, Figs. 373-374
T1917-045.claim: Argyropelecus olfersii is transformed into Sternoptyx diaphana by an oblique (shear) coordinate system whose axes are inclined at 70 degrees.
T1917-045.counterclaim: No literature test of Argyropelecus->Sternoptyx at 70 degrees was found (deep-sea pair, no landmark dataset until the repo's archival landmarking). Open in the literature; repo-tested 2026.

T1917-046.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish II), pp. 749, Figs. 375-376
T1917-046.claim: Deforming the rectilinear coordinates of a typical Scarus into (approximately) coaxial circles gives 'a very good outline' of Pomacanthus.
T1917-046.literature_citation: Bookstein, F.L. (1978), as discussed in the repo's validating script: Thompson 'drew the grids by hand and left no instructions for fitting them'
T1917-046.counterclaim: No published *quantitative* test of Scarus->Pomacanthus existed before this repo's (the audit states: 'there is still no published value to compare against -- nobody has fitted this pair'). The literature counterclaim is methodological only: an unfitted hand grid is not evidence. The quantitative refutation (Mobius ~1%, outline IoU worse than no deformation) is REPO 2026, not literature -- keep the two apart.
T1917-046.quantitative_margin: Literature: none (no numbers). Repo 2026: see pass2 -- do not cite the repo numbers as 'the literature'

T1917-047.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish II, text), pp. 749, Figs. 375-376 (text)
T1917-047.claim: The 'still more bizarre outlines of other fishes of the same family of Chaetodonts' correspond to small variations in the values of the constants of the coaxial curves.
T1917-047.counterclaim: No literature test of the 'small variations in the constants' sentence was found. Repo 2026 tested the variance half (median 35% over 54 Chaetodon spp.); the constants half was still open at registry time and is the cheapest item in the whole programme.

T1917-048.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish III), pp. 750, Figs. 377-380
T1917-048.claim: Polyprion, Pseudopriacanthus (Pristigenys) altus, Scorpaena and Antigonia capros are related by a fan/divergent-convergent coordinate transformation.
T1917-048.counterclaim: No literature test of the Polyprion->Antigonia fan series was found. Open in the literature; repo-tested 2026 at landmark level.

T1917-049.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish IV), pp. 751, Figs. 381-382
T1917-049.claim: Diodon is transformed into Orthagoriscus (Mola mola) by deforming verticals into concentric circles and horizontals into approximately hyperbolic curves.
T1917-049.counterclaim: No literature test of Diodon->Mola by concentric circles/hyperbolae was found. Open in the literature; repo-tested 2026 at landmark level.

T1917-050.citation_thompson_1917: Thompson (1917), Ch. XVII (fish, generalisation), pp. 748-751, Figs. 373-382
T1917-050.claim: IMPLIED GENERALISATION tested by this repo (not a sentence of Thompson's): the four fish families above describe related-fish form difference generally, across taxa and evolutionary time.
T1917-050.who_and_when: This row is a 2026 repo generalisation, not a 1917 claim and not literature
T1917-050.counterclaim: Not applicable to the literature: Thompson never made this generalisation in this form. Its nearest literature relatives are Bookstein (1977) (method intractable) and Scholtz et al. (2020) (simple transformations only). Cite it only as 'Dietz/repo (2026)'.
T1917-050.quantitative_margin: Repo 2026: intrageneric median 48.0% explained, 54.2% reach noise floor; interfamily only 0.3% reach the floor; horizon ~45-50 Myr

T1917-051.claim: The skulls of crocodiles (C. porosus, C. americanus, Notosuchus terrestris) are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation.
T1917-051.literature_citation: Crocodylian cranial GM is an active literature (e.g. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.14fn1) but is not framed as a test of Thompson's Fig. 383
T1917-051.counterclaim: No published test of Thompson's crocodile-skull transformation was found. The data to do it have existed since at least 2013 (dryad.14fn1) -- the gap is framing, not data.

T1917-052.claim: The pelvic/shoulder girdles of dinosaurs and plesiosaurs (Stegosaurus, Brontosaurus; Cryptocleidus etc.) are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation.
T1917-052.counterclaim: No literature test found. Fossil girdle transformations remain illustrations.

T1917-053.claim: The skulls of Dimorphodon and Pteranodon are related by coordinate transformation.
T1917-053.counterclaim: No literature test found (n=2 as stated; needs a clade frame to become testable).

T1917-054.claim: The pelves of Archaeopteryx and Apatornis (after Heilmann) and intermediate configurations can be found by interpolation between coordinate-transformed forms - i.e. interpolated grids generate biologically real intermediate forms.
T1917-054.literature_citation: Bookstein (1989) IEEE TPAMI 11:567-585; Rohlf's tps software literature (from 1990)
T1917-054.counterclaim: Heilmann's interpolation idea became standard machinery (TPS interpolation between landmark configurations is exactly how morphometricians now generate intermediates), so the *method* was vindicated by adoption. The *biological* claim -- that grid-interpolated forms are the real intermediate forms -- is only testable against fossils, and the literature does not test it on Heilmann's bird pelves.

T1917-055.claim: The skulls of rhinoceroses and their allies (Hyrachyus, Aceratherium, Titanotherium, tapir, horse, rabbit comparisons after Osborn) differ by coordinate transformation of a common skull diagram.
T1917-055.literature_citation: Osborn's rhinoceros/horse skull series are historically famous; no Thompson-transformation test of them was found

T1917-056.claim: The skull of Eohippus (Hyracotherium) is transformed into that of Equus by coordinate deformation, with actual and hypothetical intermediates (after Heilmann) lying on the transformation.
T1917-056.literature_citation: Equid skull evolution has a modern GM literature (e.g. Dryad 10.5061/dryad.crjdfn3g3, 'horses deviate from a pervasive pattern of skull shape evolution') -- its very title signals that horse skulls do NOT follow the simple pervasive pattern, but it is not a test of Thompson's Eohippus->Equus grid
T1917-056.counterclaim: No direct Thompson test found. Closest literature is suggestive-counter (horses as pattern-breakers), not a verdict on Fig. 401-402.

T1917-057.claim: Human scapulae of differing form (after Dwight) are comparable/transformable by the coordinate method.
T1917-057.counterclaim: No literature test found. Weak claim, low payoff either way.

T1917-058.claim: The human skull, inscribed in Cartesian coordinates and deformed, gives the skulls of chimpanzee, baboon and dog: ape/human skull difference is a whole-diagram transformation (notably of the facial/cranial proportions).
T1917-058.literature_citation: Bookstein (1977) Math. Biosci. 34:177-219 (general); primate cranial GM literature is large but not Thompson-framed
T1917-058.counterclaim: No published test of human->chimpanzee/baboon/dog skull transformation as Thompson drew it (Figs. 404-408) was found, despite abundant primate landmark data. Open -- and the most visible untested skull claim in the book.

T1917-059.claim: (Restatement) Form is not exhaustively explained by natural selection on independent parts; physical/mathematical law constrains the forms available to evolution.
T1917-059.counterclaim: Restatement of T1917-002: the literature's verdict is the constraint/selection synthesis, not a win for either 1917 or a purely adaptationist reading.
